description: Chess learning library used for hint coverage scoring.

entries.name: Line
entries.definition: A path of squares in one direction, like a file, rank, or diagonal.

entries.name: Clear
entries.definition: To move a piece away so another piece has room to attack.

entries.name: Guard
entries.definition: A piece that protects another piece or square.

entries.name: Loose Piece
entries.definition: A piece that is not defended and can often be won.

entries.name: Tempo Move
entries.definition: A move that improves your position while forcing a reply.

entries.name: Pin
entries.definition: A piece cannot move because moving would expose a more valuable piece behind it.

entries.name: Fork
entries.definition: One move attacks two or more enemy targets at the same time.

entries.name: Skewer
entries.definition: A more valuable piece is attacked and must move, exposing a less valuable piece behind it.

entries.name: Discovered Attack
entries.definition: Moving one piece reveals an attack from another piece behind it.

entries.name: Discovered Check
entries.definition: A discovered attack where the revealed attack is on the king.

entries.name: Double Check
entries.definition: The king is checked by two pieces at once.

entries.name: X-Ray Attack
entries.definition: Pressure passes through a piece to attack a target behind it.

entries.name: Deflection
entries.definition: A defending piece is forced away from an important square or duty.

entries.name: Attraction
entries.definition: A piece is lured to a square where it can be exploited.

entries.name: Decoy
entries.definition: A piece is tempted to move to a bad square by bait.

entries.name: Interference
entries.definition: A line between defending pieces is blocked so they cannot support each other.

entries.name: Clearance
entries.definition: A piece moves away to clear a line or square for another piece.

entries.name: Removal of Defender
entries.definition: A key defending piece is removed so a target becomes vulnerable.

entries.name: Overloading
entries.definition: A defender is forced to guard too many threats at once.

entries.name: Zwischenzug
entries.definition: An in-between move is played before the expected move.

entries.name: Quiet Move
entries.definition: A non-forcing move that creates a hidden or stronger threat.

entries.name: Sacrifice
entries.definition: Material is given up to gain a bigger strategic or tactical reward.

entries.name: Exchange Sacrifice
entries.definition: A rook is given for a minor piece to gain initiative or position.

entries.name: Greek Gift Sacrifice
entries.definition: A bishop sacrifice on the king-side to open a king attack.

entries.name: Smothered Mate
entries.definition: Checkmate where the king is trapped by its own pieces, often by a knight.

entries.name: Back-Rank Mate
entries.definition: Mate delivered on the back rank when the king has no escape squares.

entries.name: Anastasia Mate
entries.definition: A mating pattern using rook/queen with knight support against a trapped king.

entries.name: Arabian Mate
entries.definition: A mating pattern with rook and knight coordinating against a cornered king.

entries.name: Boden Mate
entries.definition: Mate delivered by crossing bishops controlling escape squares.

entries.name: Dovetail Mate
entries.definition: A queen mates the king while two adjacent escape squares are blocked.

entries.name: Hook Mate
entries.definition: A king trapped near a pawn structure is mated by heavy-piece coordination.

entries.name: Mating Net
entries.definition: A setup where the king is gradually stripped of all escape squares.

entries.name: Ladder Mate
entries.definition: Two major pieces force the king to the edge rank by rank.

entries.name: Legal's Mate
entries.definition: A classic opening trap where a queen sacrifice enables a mating attack.

entries.name: Fool's Mate
entries.definition: The fastest possible checkmate after severe opening weakening.

entries.name: Scholar's Mate
entries.definition: A beginner mating attack on the weak f7/f2 square.

entries.name: Underpromotion
entries.definition: Promoting a pawn to a piece other than a queen for tactical reasons.

entries.name: Promotion
entries.definition: A pawn reaches the last rank and becomes another piece.

entries.name: Passed Pawn
entries.definition: A pawn with no opposing pawns in front of it on its file or adjacent files.

entries.name: Outside Passed Pawn
entries.definition: A passed pawn far from the king-side action used as a distraction.

entries.name: Connected Passed Pawns
entries.definition: Adjacent passed pawns that support each other's advance.

entries.name: Pawn Break
entries.definition: A pawn push or exchange designed to open lines and change structure.

entries.name: Pawn Structure
entries.definition: The arrangement of pawns, which defines strengths, weaknesses, and plans.

entries.name: Isolated Pawn
entries.definition: A pawn with no friendly pawns on adjacent files.

entries.name: Doubled Pawns
entries.definition: Two pawns of the same side on one file.

entries.name: Backward Pawn
entries.definition: A pawn that cannot safely advance and often needs protection.

entries.name: Open File
entries.definition: A file with no pawns, ideal for rook or queen activity.

entries.name: Semi-Open File
entries.definition: A file with no friendly pawns but enemy pawns still present.

entries.name: Outpost
entries.definition: A protected square in enemy territory where a piece cannot be chased by pawns.

entries.name: Weak Square
entries.definition: A square that cannot be controlled by pawns and can be occupied by pieces.

entries.name: Weakness
entries.definition: A target in the position such as a loose piece, weak pawn, or exposed king.

entries.name: Initiative
entries.definition: The ability to force the opponent to react to your threats.

entries.name: Tempo
entries.definition: A single move; gaining tempo means improving while forcing the opponent.

entries.name: Prophylaxis
entries.definition: Preventing the opponent's plan before it becomes dangerous.

entries.name: Piece Activity
entries.definition: How effectively pieces control squares and create threats.

entries.name: Coordination
entries.definition: How well your pieces support each other.

entries.name: King Safety
entries.definition: The security of the king from immediate and long-term threats.

entries.name: Development
entries.definition: Bringing pieces from their starting squares to active squares.

entries.name: Center Control
entries.definition: Influencing key central squares to gain mobility and space.

entries.name: Space Advantage
entries.definition: Having more room for your pieces, often restricting opponent movement.

entries.name: Opposite-Side Castling
entries.definition: Both kings castle on opposite wings, often leading to sharp attacks.

entries.name: Castling
entries.definition: A king safety move that also develops the rook.

entries.name: Fianchetto
entries.definition: Developing a bishop to the long diagonal after moving the adjacent pawn.

entries.name: Opposition
entries.definition: Kings face each other with one square between; one side controls key entry.

entries.name: Triangulation
entries.definition: A maneuver to lose a tempo and transfer move obligation to the opponent.

entries.name: Zugzwang
entries.definition: Any legal move worsens the player's position.

entries.name: Fortress
entries.definition: A defensive setup that cannot be broken despite material deficit.

entries.name: Perpetual Check
entries.definition: Repeated checks force a draw because escape is impossible.

entries.name: Stalemate
entries.definition: Side to move has no legal moves and is not in check, resulting in a draw.

entries.name: Opposite-Colored Bishops
entries.definition: Bishops on different colors often increase drawing chances.

entries.name: Lucena Position
entries.definition: A key rook endgame winning method with a bridge-building maneuver.

entries.name: Philidor Position
entries.definition: A key rook endgame drawing method by active rook defense.

entries.name: Check
entries.definition: A direct attack on the king that must be answered immediately.

entries.name: Checkmate
entries.definition: The king is in check and has no legal escape.

entries.name: Capture
entries.definition: Removing an enemy piece by moving onto its square.

entries.name: Threat
entries.definition: A move that creates a future danger the opponent must respect.

entries.name: Defender
entries.definition: A piece that protects a square, piece, or king.

entries.name: Attacker
entries.definition: A piece actively creating pressure or direct threats.

entries.name: Escape Square
entries.definition: A legal square the king can move to avoid danger.

entries.name: File
entries.definition: A vertical column of squares on the chessboard.

entries.name: Rank
entries.definition: A horizontal row of squares on the chessboard.

entries.name: Diagonal
entries.definition: A line of same-colored squares connected corner to corner.

entries.name: Center
entries.definition: The central squares and surrounding area that influence piece activity.

entries.name: Long Diagonal
entries.definition: A diagonal that stretches across much of the board and boosts bishop power.

entries.name: Line Opening
entries.definition: Opening files or diagonals to activate pieces and launch tactics.

entries.name: King Walk
entries.definition: An endgame king march to support pawns or invade key squares.

entries.name: Rook Lift
entries.definition: Moving a rook up a file then across a rank to join an attack.

entries.name: Battery
entries.definition: Two aligned pieces support each other on the same line of attack.

entries.name: Bishop Pair
entries.definition: Having both bishops often gives strong long-range control.

entries.name: Minor Piece Endgame
entries.definition: An endgame where bishops and/or knights decide key plans.

entries.name: Rook Endgame
entries.definition: An endgame where rooks are the main active pieces.

entries.name: Queen Endgame
entries.definition: An endgame where queens remain and perpetual threats are common.

entries.name: King and Pawn Endgame
entries.definition: A pure endgame where king activity and pawn races are central.
